findings.title: upsampled_count() not registered in errors dataset
findings.body: The SnQLFunction `upsampled_count` is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter, but `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emits `"upsampled_count() as count"` regardless of which dataset is being queried. When the errors dataset is used (which is the primary use case for error upsampling, and is the dataset that `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for unconditionally), the query will fail at the Snuba layer with an unknown-function error. The function must also be registered in the errors dataset's function converter.

findings.title: Cache invalidation function is never called
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but no code anywhere calls it. Because the cache TTL is 60 seconds, when a project is removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` (e.g. during a rollback), that project will continue to receive upsampled `count()` results for up to 60 seconds, producing incorrect (inflated) counts in production. The docstring acknowledges that 'allowlist changes are infrequent' but does not justify serving incorrect data after removals. The cache should be invalidated synchronously when the option changes, or the option lookup itself should not be cached.

findings.title: _is_error_focused_query uses substring matching despite claiming caution
findings.body: The implementation does `'event.type:error' in query` (lowercased substring), and the docstring claims it was 'Reduced to only check for event.type:error to err on the side of caution.' Substring matching is the opposite of cautious: `NOT event.type:error` matches (the query excludes errors yet upsampling will be applied), `event.type:error_handled` matches (a non-error event type is treated as an error), and `message:"event.type:error occurred"` matches. This will cause `sum(sample_weight)` upsampled counts to be returned for queries that are explicitly about non-error events, corrupting customer-facing time series. The check should tokenize and parse the query (or at minimum require word boundaries / absence of a leading `NOT`).

findings.title: Unrelated breaking change to user-facing error text
findings.body: The error message for `topEvents <= 0` was changed from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. This is a user-facing 400 response that has nothing to do with the PR's stated purpose (upsampled error counts). It silently changes a documented API contract, will break any tests, alerts, or downstream consumers that pattern-match the message, and should be reverted or split into a separate PR.

findings.title: setUp overwrites self.user after login_as uses it
findings.body: In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, `self.login_as(user=self.user)` and `self.authed_user = self.user` are executed before `self.user = self.create_user()`. The login and stored `authed_user` reference the parent `APITestCase`'s user, then `self.user` is reassigned to a freshly created user that was never logged in. The `tags` on stored events reference this new `self.user`/`self.user2` (which are different identities than the authenticated principal), so the test fixture is internally inconsistent and any tag-based filtering or permission check against the new users will not behave as intended. Reorder setUp so users are created before login_as, or stop reassigning self.user.

findings.title: Organization parameter unused in allowlist check
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` accepts `organization: Organization` but never references it. The allowlist `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is treated as a single global list of project IDs with no org scoping. If two organizations share a project ID space (e.g. in tests, or in any multi-tenant view of the option), a match in the allowlist could trigger upsampling for projects in the wrong organization. Either drop the unused parameter or actually verify each project_id belongs to `organization`.

findings.title: Transform only matches literal count(), misses aliased and other count variants
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only matches the exact stripped/lowercased string `count()`. It will not transform `count() as total`, `count_if(...)`, `count_unique(...)`, `count_web_vitals(...)`, etc. Any aggregation that semantically counts events but isn't literal `count()` will return non-upsampled counts in the same response, producing mixed results where some y-axes are upsampled and others are not for the same time bucket. The match should also handle aliased forms and at minimum `count_if`-style aggregates for errors, or the contract should be clearly documented.

findings.title: Main public function and cache invalidation are untested
findings.body: The test file covers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, `_is_error_focused_query`, and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, but never exercises the main entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (cache hit/miss, cache-key determinism, interaction with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and never tests `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Given the cache-related concerns above, these are exactly the paths that need direct test coverage.

findings.title: Hard-coded count==10 assumes undocumented sample_weight semantics
findings.body: The assertions `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10` rely on `sum(sample_weight)` producing 10 when `client_sample_rate` is 0.1. That is only true if the Snuba `sample_weight` column is precomputed as `1/sample_rate` rather than equal to `sample_rate`. The factory change only sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"] = float(client_sample_rate)`; nothing in this PR guarantees that `sample_weight` in Snuba equals `1/sample_rate`. If `sample_weight` is NULL or equals `sample_rate`, the test will silently produce wrong counts in CI and the assertion will fail or, worse, pass against a different column. Either add an explicit comment/schema check documenting the invariant, or compute the expected value from whatever mapping actually exists.

findings.title: Factory silently overwrites event sample_rate with context value
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` unconditionally assigns `normalized_data["sample_rate"] = float(client_sample_rate)` whenever the `error_sampling` context is present. `sample_rate` is a standard SDK-provided field on events; overwriting it from a separate `error_sampling` context (which carries a different semantic — client-side reporting rate, not SDK capture rate) can corrupt downstream consumers that read `sample_rate` for ingest sampling math. It should only set the field when the event doesn't already carry a `sample_rate`, or write to a distinct field. The two bare `except Exception: pass` blocks additionally hide all errors including programming mistakes.

findings.title: Cache returns truthy cached_result but stores strict booleans inconsistently
findings.body: `cache.get(cache_key)` returns `cached_result` which was stored as a Python `bool` (`is_eligible`), but the return path does `return cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`. If `is_eligible` was `False`, the cached value is `False` and the short-circuit returns `False`, skipping the dataset check — this means a request whose project set is not allowlisted will never even consult the dataset/transactions filter, which is fine. However, if the cache backend ever returns a non-bool truthy value (e.g. some serializers wrap booleans), the `and` chain would produce unexpected types. More importantly, the dataset/sample_weight check is intentionally re-evaluated on every cache hit even though it has no dependency on the cached value's inputs, so the caching only saves the `options.get` and the per-project allowlist scan — but the cache key itself varies by project set, so hit rate for any given key is low. This negates the claimed performance benefit.
